name: Ashley Moody
pollingDetails: UNF Public Opinion Research Lab (Oct 12-19, 1,471 likely voters, MoE 2.8): Moody 49%, Nixon 45%. Mason-Dixon/NBC6 (Sept 28-Oct 1, 625 RV): Moody 50%, Nixon 40%, Gillespie 2%. Stetson (Oct 1-9, RV): Moody 52%, Nixon 41%. St. Pete Polls (Sept 15-17) had it tied 45-45. Poliwave average through Oct 23: Moody +6.5, rated Likely Republican; Democrats have not won a Florida Senate race since 2012.
raised: $14.5M campaign committee ($816K COH, FEC pre-general through Oct 14 2026); Tampa Bay Times (Oct 17 2026) puts her cycle total across all committees at $20.6M with $7.2M cash entering October
backers: Stronger Safer Nation super PAC (approx. $3M in anti-Nixon ads per Tampa Bay Times, plus $2.5M from Citadel founder Ken Griffin per Miami Herald), Senate Leadership Fund, Associated Industries of Florida, Florida Professional Firefighters, Florida sheriffs and state attorneys
lgbtqDetails: Scored 0 on the HRC 119th Congressional Scorecard (Oct 2026). As Attorney General she sued the Biden administration over Title IX protections for LGBTQ+ students and over gender-affirming care; in the Senate she championed the bill to bar transgender athletes from women's sports and said its vote made Republicans 'the new party of women' (Florida Politics).
platform: Appointed by Gov. DeSantis in January 2025 to fill Marco Rubio's seat after six years as Florida Attorney General and prior service as a Hillsborough circuit judge and federal prosecutor. Runs on border security and support for ICE, backing President Trump's agenda, crime and law enforcement, tax cuts, and opposition to 'socialism'; she declined to debate Nixon.
controversy: Hope Florida: PolitiFact (Oct 22 2026) and WLRN report that her AG office approved the 2024 Centene Medicaid settlement that steered $10M to the Hope Florida Foundation, money that then flowed to political committees fighting Amendment 3; experts told PolitiFact she is responsible for her office's actions though no charges were filed and a grand jury's findings were expunged. WUSF (Oct 1 2026) reports Democrats attacking her for skipping debates and town halls.
endorsements: Donald Trump, Sen. Rick Scott, Reps. Byron Donalds, Gus Bilirakis, Vern Buchanan, Kat Cammack, Laurel Lee and most of the Florida GOP delegation, Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson, 15 state attorneys, Palm Beach Sheriff Ric Bradshaw, Associated Industries of Florida, Florida Professional Firefighters
primaryResult: won Aug 18 GOP primary with about 79.6% over Chris Gleason, Ernest Rivera and Neelam Taneja Perry (Fox 13, 99% reporting)

name: Angie Nixon
pollingDetails: UNF (Oct 12-19, 1,471 LV): Nixon 45%, Moody 49%, with Nixon leading independents by 15. Mason-Dixon/NBC6 (Sept 28-Oct 1, 625 RV): Nixon 40%, Moody 50%; Tampa Bay region tied 44-44. Stetson (Oct 1-9): Nixon 41%, Moody 52%. St. Pete Polls (Sept 15-17) showed a 45-45 tie. Poliwave average through Oct 23: Moody +6.5.
raised: $8.5M total through Sept 30 2026 with $4.5M COH (Tampa Bay Times, Oct 17 2026, all committees); outraised Moody in Q3 ($7.6M-$7.9M vs $5.8M); FEC candidate-committee page shows $3.27M COH through Oct 14 2026
backers: Small-dollar donors (campaign says no corporate PAC money), Common Defense, Higher Heights for America PAC, progressive national figures; Votelog tracker shows about $2.8M in post-primary outside spending supporting her and $7.7M opposing
lgbtqDetails: Endorsed by Equality Florida Action, Inc. for U.S. Senate (Sept 2026); her platform pledges to protect LGBTQ+ neighbors and she spoke on the House floor in defense of trans people during the 2023 expansion of the Parental Rights in Education law (per Daily Wire coverage). Her Jacksonville bookstore, Cafe Resistance, hosts LGBTQ community events.
platform: Jacksonville state representative since 2020, former labor organizer and small business owner, and a member of the Democratic Socialists of America since June 2026. Runs on Medicare for All (short term: restoring enhanced ACA tax credits), raising the federal minimum wage, repealing the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act, a moratorium on new data centers, criminal justice reform, and opposition to the 2026 Iran war.
controversy: Axios Miami and NBC6 (Oct 27 2026) report bipartisan backlash after she declined in a CBS interview to call Cuba's government a dictatorship, which she later walked back. The Hill reports she defended saying Moody should face jail over Hope Florida. The Washington Free Beacon (Oct 27) reports a National Legal and Policy Center complaint alleging roughly $270K in missing charitable funds tied to her Cafe Resistance nonprofit, which is an allegation by a conservative watchdog, not a finding. In May 2026 the Florida House Rules and Ethics Committee reprimanded her for using a megaphone during the redistricting debate, and she was arrested at a sit-in at Gov. DeSantis' office (Wikipedia, citing news reports).
endorsements: Barack Obama (video, late Oct 2026, per Politico), Bernie Sanders, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Ilhan Omar, Maxwell Frost, Anna Eskamani, Equality Florida Action Inc., Common Defense, Higher Heights for America PAC
primaryResult: won Aug 18 Democratic primary 56.1% over Alexander Vindman in an upset

name: Neil J. Gillespie
pollingDetails: Mason-Dixon/NBC6 (Sept 28-Oct 1, 625 RV) had Gillespie at 2% statewide and 8% among independents; most other polls do not list him.
raised: Not found (FEC committee C00943399 registered; no financial totals located)
lgbtqDetails: No statements or record on LGBTQ+ issues found.
platform: Ocala-area pro se litigant and self-described justice-reform activist who runs the 'Justice Network' blog; perennial candidate (2020, 2024 and 2028 presidential committees, a run for Ocala mayor). Campaign themes are court and legal-profession accountability, separation of powers, and complaints about the FEC and DOJ; he qualified by petition as NPA on April 24, 2026.
controversy: None significant reported; Politics1 describes him as a frequent candidate, and Ballotpedia notes he was disqualified from Florida's 2024 presidential ballot.
primaryResult: n/a (NPA candidates qualify directly for the general election)

name: Anna Paulina Luna
pollingDetails: No independent public poll. Hart Research for House Majority PAC (D) Aug 25-27: Gray 51%, Luna 46% head-to-head, or Gray 44 / Luna 43 / D'Arrigo 7 three-way (MoE 4.4). Fabrizio Lee (R) Aug 4-6: Luna 49%, Gray 41%. GQR (D) Aug 4-6: Luna 47%, Gray 44%. Florida Politics (mid-Oct) reported a Hakeem Jeffries-aligned PAC poll again showing Gray ahead. Cook rates the seat Likely R; Inside Elections moved it to Lean R on Oct 1. The redrawn district voted Trump +13 in 2024 and Luna won by about 10 in 2024.
raised: About $4.1M cycle receipts, $1.08M COH as of Sept 30 2026 (FEC Q3 via Florida Politics); pre-general report shows roughly $747K COH as of Oct 14 2026 (Quiver/MAHA Action). Raised about $856K in Q3 vs Gray's $1.34M.
backers: Club for Growth Action (approx. $300K pro-Luna ads earlier in 2026), MAHA Action, Trump-aligned small-dollar network, Congressional Leadership Fund-aligned groups (specific CD 13 general-election IE totals not found)
lgbtqDetails: HRC Congressional Scorecard: 0 for the 118th Congress and 10 for the 119th (Oct 2026). Per Your Rep's Record she did not cosponsor the Equality Act and voted for H.R. 498 to bar Medicaid coverage of gender-affirming care; Trump's Truth Social endorsement attacks Gray over transgender issues.
platform: Two-term Air Force veteran and former Turning Point USA figure who chairs the House Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets and pushed proxy voting for new parents. Runs on Trump's agenda, border security, the SAVE Act, a congressional stock-trading ban, pesticide-liability reform, and MAHA health positions.
controversy: Tampa Bay Times (July 20 and Aug 3 2026) summarized a Wall Street Journal report that she may have passed insider information to influencer Rogan O'Handley for Polymarket bets; the Times later reported DOJ never received a referral and Luna's lawyers sent the paper a cease-and-desist. Gray's ads cite the story and Luna's campaign sent Gray a cease-and-desist (Floridian Press, Sept 2026). Raw Story reported on her husband's stock in a stem-cell company given her anti-abortion stance; Luna's office denied any affiliation.
endorsements: Donald Trump, MAHA Action, Club for Growth, Ric Grenell, House Freedom Caucus allies
primaryResult: unopposed in Aug 18 GOP primary (NBC News lists the race as uncontested)

name: Leela Gray
pollingDetails: No independent public poll. Hart Research for House Majority PAC (D) Aug 25-27: Gray 51%, Luna 46% head-to-head (MoE 4.4); 44-43-7 with D'Arrigo included. GQR (D) Aug 4-6: Luna 47%, Gray 44%. Fabrizio Lee (R) Aug 4-6: Luna 49%, Gray 41%. Ratings: Cook Likely R, Inside Elections Lean R (Oct 1). Florida Politics notes the last two Democrats to poll this well against Luna lost by about 9 points.
raised: About $2.57M cycle total, $601K COH as of Sept 30 2026 (FEC Q3 via Florida Politics); $1.34M raised Jul 30-Sep 30 and about $656K COH as of Oct 14 2026 (pre-general, via Quiver)
backers: EMILY's List, DCCC Red to Blue, House Majority PAC, VoteVets, AFL-CIO Florida and West Central Florida Labor Council, 1199 SEIU, UAW Region 8, Teamsters Local 79, IBEW Local 915, Planned Parenthood Action Fund, League of Conservation Voters, Moms Demand Action, MoveOn, NewDem Action Fund, Blue Dog PAC
lgbtqDetails: No votes or LGBTQ-specific statements found; her endorsement page lists no LGBTQ+ organization and Equality Florida Action's first-wave congressional endorsements (Sept 15 2026) and voter guide do not list a CD 13 pick. Endorsed by Pete Buttigieg and mainstream Democratic groups.
platform: Retired Army brigadier general with 30-plus years of service, a Stetson law degree and nonprofit governance experience; first-time candidate recruited after Whitney Fox's 2024 loss. Runs on cost of living, taking on insurers and corporations over premiums, a middle-class tax cut, protecting Social Security and veterans' care, and attacking Luna over a 'culture of corruption'.
controversy: Luna's counter-ads accuse Gray of hypocrisy over her own stock investments and Luna's lawyers sent her campaign a cease-and-desist over the insider-trading ad (Tampa Bay Times, Sept 15 2026; Floridian Press). A Prediction Edge profile says local coverage described her as identifying as pro-life, which could not be confirmed in primary reporting.
endorsements: Tampa Bay Times editorial board, EMILY's List, Sen. Mark Kelly, Gov. Abigail Spanberger, Pete Buttigieg, Reps. Kathy Castor, Katherine Clark, Steny Hoyer, Jason Crow, Seth Moulton, Maxwell Frost, Lois Frankel, Alex Sink, Whitney Fox, VoteVets, Alliance for Retired Americans, Florida AFL-CIO, Planned Parenthood Action Fund
primaryResult: won Aug 18 Democratic primary about 65% over Brandt Robinson (26%) and John Liccione (9%)

name: Tony D'Arrigo
pollingDetails: Only the Hart Research/House Majority PAC poll (Aug 25-27) tested him, at 7% in a three-way ballot with Gray 44% and Luna 43%. He received 27 write-in votes in the 2024 CD 13 race.
raised: Not found (FEC shows no 2025-26 financial summary for committee C00868547; a July 2024 report showed $13,500 raised)
backers: None identified; says he takes no party or corporate money
lgbtqDetails: No statements or record on LGBTQ+ issues found in his Tampa Bay 28 questionnaire or Ballotpedia survey.
platform: New Jersey-raised hospitality manager, small business owner and author who moved to Tampa Bay in 2014 and ran as a write-in for this seat in 2024. His top issue is health care after his own cancer diagnosis: expand coverage, protect the ACA, de-privatize hospitals and reform costs; he pitches himself as a non-career politician who votes issue by issue.
primaryResult: n/a (NPA candidates qualify directly for the general election)

name: Sydney Gruters
pollingDetails: No independent public poll. Public Policy Polling (D-sponsored) Oct 1-2, 530 RV: Gruters 43%, Kirschner 39%. SEA Research for the Kirschner campaign, Aug 25-29, n=400: Kirschner 40%, Gruters 39%. Ratings: Cook moved the seat from Safe R to Likely R on Oct 17; Inside Elections and Sabato Likely R. Buchanan won the old district by 19 in 2024; the 2026 map adds south Pinellas and parts of Polk.
raised: $1.62M raised, $1.37M spent, $252K COH (FEC pre-general through Oct 14 2026, via Midterm Monday); $486K raised Jul 30-Sep 30 with $616K COH on Sept 30 (Florida Politics, Oct 2026)
backers: Conservatives for American Excellence super PAC (approx. $1.04M supporting her plus $705K attacking Kirschner), Foundations PAC, Winning for Women, Maggie's List, Turning Point Action, House GOP leadership PACs, SpaceX corporate PAC (Tampa Bay Times, Oct 21 2026); outside support totals about $1.78M per FEC Schedule E
lgbtqDetails: No votes, statements or LGBTQ-group endorsements found; her platform emphasizes immigration, taxes and Trump alignment, and she is backed by Turning Point Action.
platform: First-time candidate, former district director for Rep. Greg Steube and Buchanan staffer, and until recently executive director of the New College Foundation; wife of state Sen. and RNC Chair Joe Gruters. Runs on cutting taxes and costs, working with Trump and ICE on immigration, election security, curbing overdevelopment, veterans' benefits, and protecting Social Security and Medicare.
controversy: Primary rivals Eddie Speir and Ed Pope said she had no record and owed Trump's endorsement to her husband's connections (Bradenton Times). Kirschner's campaign accused her of benefiting from roughly $2.5M in AI-generated super PAC ads it called false (Tampa Bay Times, Oct 21 2026). Her New College Foundation tenure drew a former-board-member demand letter seeking an audit of restricted donor funds and a 2025 scholarship lawsuit (WUSF, Herald-Tribune); she called critics' claims baseless.
endorsements: Donald Trump, Rep. Vern Buchanan, Sen. Rick Scott, Speaker Mike Johnson, Rep. Anna Paulina Luna, all six sheriffs in the district, Winning for Women, Maggie's List, Turning Point Action
primaryResult: won Aug 18 GOP primary with about 63% over Eddie Speir and Ed Pope

name: Kelly Kirschner
pollingDetails: No independent public poll. Public Policy Polling (D-sponsored) Oct 1-2, 530 RV: Kirschner 39%, Gruters 43%. His own SEA Research poll (Aug 25-29, n=400) had him ahead 40-39 and leading 44-43 after respondents heard candidate profiles. Cook rates the seat Likely R (from Safe R, Oct 17); the DCCC lists it among its 'Districts in Play' but has not spent directly.
raised: $876K raised, $615K spent, $261K COH (FEC pre-general through Oct 14 2026, via Midterm Monday); $455K raised Jul 30-Sep 30 with $353K COH on Sept 30 (Florida Politics)
backers: Grassroots donors (no corporate PAC money), Equality Florida Action Inc., a supporting committee that received $10K from Alex Vindman's former campaign (Tampa Bay Times); outside support negligible per FEC Schedule E while Conservatives for American Excellence spent about $705K against him
lgbtqDetails: Listed as Equality Florida Action, Inc.'s endorsed candidate for District 16 in its 2026 pro-equality voter guide; no contrary record found.
platform: Former Sarasota mayor and city commissioner (youngest in city history), Georgetown graduate, Peace Corps volunteer in Guatemala, former Eckerd College vice president and UnidosNow leader. Runs on a 'Scalpel Plan' to cut contractor markups and protect Social Security, Medicare and veterans' care, fighting predatory developers and monopolies, opposing taxpayer-funded political ads, and criticizing the New College takeover of USF Sarasota-Manatee.
controversy: None significant reported. Trump attacked him on Truth Social in late October (Bradenton Journal).
endorsements: Equality Florida Action Inc., Bradenton Times editorial board, former Rep. Dan Miller and Manatee Commissioner George Kruse ('Republicans for Kirschner'), former St. Petersburg Mayor Rick Kriseman, DCCC 'Districts in Play' designation
primaryResult: won Aug 18 Democratic primary with just over 43% in a five-way field over Jonathan Harris, Tamika Lyles, Glenn Pearson and Jan Schneider

name: Mark Davis
pollingDetails: Not included in the PPP or SEA Research polls of the district; no public poll has tested him.
raised: Not found (FEC candidate ID H6FL06365; no financial totals located)
lgbtqDetails: No statements or record on LGBTQ+ issues found; his site features 'No Kings' and 'ICE OUT' imagery (WGCU).
platform: Air Force veteran (2005-2013) and small business owner who describes himself as a moderate Democrat and fiscal conservative running without a party. Criticizes tariffs, supports single-payer health care, wants to cut everyday costs, and pledges to take a sharply reduced congressional salary.
controversy: WWSB/ABC7 and Tampa Bay 28 reported he was arrested July 28 2026 in Parrish for obstruction without violence after deputies said he pushed past investigators during a court-ordered DCF welfare check on his children; he posted $500 bond, deputies found the children safe, and he called the complaint retaliation for criticizing Trump and DeSantis. No reporting on the case's disposition was found.
primaryResult: n/a (NPA candidates qualify directly for the general election)
